headline: Linn of Mercy Flares Anew as Fishermans Row Grows Quiet
war_summary: The past three hours have rewritten the map's temper. The Linn of Mercy, cool at our last posting, has erupted again: its Lathair ground has logged twenty flag events in the day, and hourly losses there leapt from single figures to more than a hundred men on either side, with ten of its eleven strongholds flying Colonial colors. Fishermans Row, until now the war's busiest post at forty-two events, has seen no flag move since mid-morning, its ledger reading six Colonial works to two Warden and a ruin. Weathered Expanse remains the fiercest field, thirty-four events recorded and hourly losses past a thousand Colonial and sixteen hundred Warden, its works standing five Warden against three and one demolished. Mooring County's flags have been still since late morning, yet its toll tops six hundred men an hour a side across eleven Warden-held works. Stlican Shelf quieted after a busy dawn, six Warden strongholds to three, while Stonecradle's five-to-four split endures beneath a swelling casualty roll. Callahans Passage moved no flags but bled more than a thousand men an hour to each army, and Godcrofts now counts nine Colonial works and none Warden. Day 287; no victor declared.
